text:
Liam (AE): quick help — prospect POC keeps hitting a 413 when sending full conversation + attachments in one request. They want single-call for evaluation. Body ~130KB. Endpoint: POST /v1/generate model=rw-base-8k. Any quick playbook?
Meera (SE): Can you paste the raw error from their client or gateway?
Liam (AE): client sees: 413 Payload Too Large. Gateway log we got back from their support thread:
DevBot: gateway: client 10.8.1.9 request rejected: max_payload_bytes_exceeded, length=130112, limit=102400
Zoe (SRE): Confirmed — our edge/nginx gate has 100KB body limit right now for hosted. This rejects before it reaches the runtime.
Meera (SE): Workarounds, ordered by minimal engineering:
- Use Content-Encoding: gzip (we accept compressed bodies)
- Upload conversation as a file to S3 (presigned URL) and pass the S3 object key or short pointer in the request (we have an attachment pattern in the POC docs)
- Send the recent N turns and a client-side summary of earlier context (context-rolling + summarization)
- Multipart/form-data file upload to /v1/uploads then reference 
Meera (SE): If they insist on single-call raw JSON body, only option is a dedicated sandbox with relaxed proxy limits (ops + infra).
Liam (AE): They asked whether switching to a 32k model helps.
Zoe (SRE): Bigger model window doesn't change HTTP limit. If you can get the body through, model choice affects token handling, not HTTP.
Meera (SE): Practical steps for the customer now: 1) Try gzipping payload (fast) 2) If gzipping impossible, use presigned upload + pointer 3) If they want engineering help, we can spin up a short-lived dedicated sandbox for single-call tests.
Liam (AE): Can you paste a sample presigned flow and a gzip curl I can send?
Meera (SE): Sample gzip curl:
```
echo -n '{\"model\":\"rw-base-8k\",\"input\":\"<LONG_CHAT>\"}' | gzip -c | \\n  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \\
    -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' \\
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
    --data-binary @-
```
Meera (SE): Presigned flow sketch:
1) POST /v1/uploads/initiate -> returns presigned PUT URL
2) Client PUTs the file to presigned URL (standard S3)
3) POST /v1/generate {\"model\":\"...\",\"context_url\":\"s3://bucket/key\"}
Sample multipart curl (if they prefer form upload):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \\
  -F 'file=@conversation.json'
```
Zoe (SRE): I'll validate the exact edge limit and whether our CDN layer enforces a smaller cap. If repeated 413s spike, we should alert.
ingest-bot: ticket created INF-912: investigate hosted body-size cap and add alert for >5 413s/min
Liam (AE): I'll send gzip + presigned options to the prospect. If they want a single-call demo we should quote dedicated sandbox pricing.
Meera (SE): Pricing ops note: short sandbox (2 weeks) -> we can offer eval credit modeled as a Dedicated trial; coordinate with PMM for billing code.
Liam (AE): Prospect tried gzip and it passed through — they reported 200 and tokens looked good. They're testing quality now.
Zoe (SRE): Great — capturing this in the POC runbook so AEs can send the exact commands. I'll add a short FAQ entry about the difference between HTTP limits and model context.
Meera (SE): Also adding a snippet to sales playbook: when body>80KB recommend presigned S3 or gzip as first-line.
Liam (AE): awesome, thanks all :raised_hands:
